skill_drafts.name: TF-IDF Vector Scoring
skill_drafts.description: Compute relevance scores for documents by combining term frequency, inverse document frequency, and vector normalization. Use when ranking search results or comparing document similarity in information retrieval tasks.
applicable_signals: document collection indexed with term frequencies and document frequencies
relevance ranking required for downstream presentation or filtering
contraindications: documents are very short or sparse (tf-idf may not capture meaningful signal)
query contains no meaningful terms or is empty
real-time latency is critical and precomputation of idf and document vectors is unavailable
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Extract or retrieve term frequencies (tf) for each query term in each candidate document'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Retrieve or compute inverse document frequency (idf) for each query term: idf(t) = log(N / df(t)), where N is total documents and df(t) is document frequency of term t'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Compute weighted term vector for query: qi = tf(i) × idf(i) for each term i'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Compute weighted term vector for each document: di = normalized tf(i) × idf(i), applying chosen normalization (e.g., cosine: divide by L2 norm of document vector)'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Compute relevance score as dot product: score(query, document) = Σ(qi × di)'}
{'step': 6, 'action': 'Sort documents by descending score and return ranked list with numeric scores'}
triggers: need to rank documents by relevance to a query
comparing document similarity across a collection
constraints: corpus statistics (document frequency, collection size) must be precomputed or available
term tokenization and normalization must be consistent between query and document indexing
vector normalization method (cosine, pivoted length, or other) must be chosen and applied consistently
cautions: tf-idf assumes term independence; does not capture semantic relationships or phrase structure
very long documents may be over-weighted unless length normalization is applied
rare terms receive high idf weight; ensure stopword filtering is applied upstream if needed
output_contract: Ranked list of documents with numeric relevance scores; each document paired with its query-document dot product value (cosine similarity or equivalent normalized score). Scores are comparable across documents for the same query.

metadata.prompt: For each query-document pair: (1) compute term frequency (tf) for each query term in the document; (2) compute inverse document frequency (idf) for each term across the corpus; (3) weight each term as tf × idf; (4) normalize the document vector (e.g., by cosine normalization or pivoted document length normalization); (5) compute the dot product of the query vector and normalized document vector to obtain the final relevance score. Return ranked list of documents sorted by descending score.

skill_drafts.name: Pivoted Document Length Normalization
skill_drafts.description: Adjust TF-IDF scores to account for document length bias using linear scaling with a pivot point. Apply when longer documents should not be artificially favored in relevance ranking.
applicable_signals: document collection exhibits high variance in document length
cosine normalization alone over-penalizes longer documents
relevance ranking shows length bias favoring short documents
need to balance document length as a confounding factor
contraindications: all documents in collection are similar length
document length is not a confounding factor in relevance
using BM25 or other length-aware probabilistic models already
collection is already balanced by length normalization
intervention_moves: Compute cosine-normalized score |V(d)| for each document
Determine pivot point piv from the document collection (intersection of cosine curve and y=x line)
Select slope parameter a (0 < a < 1) based on desired length sensitivity
triggers: document collection has high variance in document length; cosine normalization alone over-penalizes long documents; need to balance length bias with relevance
constraints: slope parameter a must satisfy 0 < a < 1
pivot point piv must be computed from the same document collection
input scores must be cosine-normalized before applying pivoted scaling
method assumes linear relationship between document length and score adjustment
cautions: pivot point selection is empirical; different collections may require different piv values
slope parameter a controls sensitivity; lower a reduces length bias more aggressively
this is a post-processing step; apply after initial TF-IDF computation
output_contract: Adjusted relevance scores with linear scaling applied. Each score is computed as a|V(d)| + (1-a)piv. Output includes the normalization factor and adjusted score for each document, suitable for downstream ranking or retrieval tasks.

metadata.prompt: Compute normalized relevance scores using pivoted document length normalization. For each document, apply the linear scaling formula: score_normalized = a|V(d)| + (1-a)piv, where |V(d)| is the cosine-normalized score, piv is the pivot point (intersection of cosine curve and y=x line), and a is the slope parameter (a < 1). The pivot point is typically determined empirically from the document collection. Return adjusted scores that balance length bias with relevance.

skill_drafts.name: Weighted Zone Scoring
skill_drafts.description: Assign different weights to term occurrences in different document zones (e.g., title, body, metadata) to reflect their importance. Use when document structure provides signals about term relevance.
applicable_signals: document zone boundaries are clearly defined
zone-specific term frequency data is available
contraindications: zone boundaries are unclear or unreliable
computational cost of zone parsing is prohibitive
workflow_steps: Parse document into zones (title, abstract, body, keywords, metadata)
For each query term, identify zone occurrences and extract term frequency per zone
Apply zone-specific weight multiplier to each zone's term frequency
Combine weighted contributions across all zones
triggers: documents have structured zones (title, abstract, body, keywords)
terms in certain zones are more indicative of relevance
need to boost or suppress zone-specific matches
constraints: zone weights must be pre-defined or learned from training data
zone boundaries must be reliably extractable from document structure
output_contract: Weighted term frequency values per zone; combined score reflecting zone-weighted contributions to overall relevance score

metadata.prompt: For each term in the query, identify which document zones it appears in (title, abstract, body, keywords, etc.). Apply zone-specific weights to the term frequency in each zone. Combine weighted contributions across zones to produce a final relevance score that reflects the structural importance of term matches.
